cards.front: Recall a key point about Context and Social/Historical Influences
cards.back: Context: the social, cultural, historical and political circumstances in which a play was written AND in which it is performed.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Context and Social/Historical Influences
cards.back: Original context shapes the play's meaning — An Inspector Calls (1945, set 1912) uses dramatic irony about world wars the audience knew had happened.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Context and Social/Historical Influences
cards.back: Modern production context: a director may reset a play in a different period to make contemporary connections — this changes the meaning.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Context and Social/Historical Influences
cards.back: Social influences: class, gender, race, power structures — these are reflected in and critiqued by drama.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Context and Social/Historical Influences
cards.back: Historical influences: the period's events, beliefs and values — understanding them reveals the playwright's purpose.

cards.front: What should you know about drama exam tips?
cards.back: When discussing context, always show how it SHAPES MEANING: 'The play was written in 1945 but set in 1912, creating dramatic irony — the audience knows that two world wars followed, which gives the Inspector's warning about collective responsibility greater urgency and makes the Birlings' complacency more shocking.'
Class, gender, attitudes (e.g. Reveals character motivation)
Events, politics, technology (e.g. Explains dramatic irony)
Art, philosophy, values (e.g. Explains form and style)
Playwright's life, beliefs (e.g. Reveals authorial intention)

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Context is just background information that you mention in the introduction — it doesn't really affect how you analyse the play. Correct: Context is ESSENTIAL to meaning. The playwright's choices are shaped by their social, historical and political circumstances. A play about class written in 1945 has different meaning than one written in 2025. Context exp
Explain how the social and historical context of a play you have studied shapes its meaning. How might a modern production use context to make the play relevant to a contemporary audience?

Context questions test AO1 (knowledge of the play's background) and AO2 (analysing how context shapes meaning). In both sections of the written exam, contextual understanding elevates your response from basic description to perceptive analysis. Context explains WHY — and the 'why' questions carry the highest marks.

Understanding the context in which a play was written and first performed is essential for GCSE analysis. Social context includes the class structure, gender roles, economic conditions and cultural attitudes of the period.
